recommendation_assessment:
The main conclusion holds: do not fork the reference code or copy its checkpoints. Use it as a design reference and a source of evaluation data. I confirmed every bug the report lists by reading the source, and found one more (the i==0 branch indexing). Three things should change.

1) Start from the cleaned Dixon OLTW in pymatchmaker's develop branch (matchmaker/dp/oltw_dixon.py, OnlineTimeWarpingDixonFrame) instead of a new clean-room DP. It is Apache-2.0 and was written in Jun-Aug 2026 by the same author (jiyun.park), validated against Dixon's Java implementation. It already has every fix the report proposes: additive (1,1,2) weights, normalisation by 1+i+j, a BOTH step, best-match output and run-count limits. It also takes any reference_features matrix through a per-frame __call__. Do not depend on the PyPI package: it pins numpy<2.0 and Python<3.13, which conflicts with librosa 1.0 and synctoolbox 1.4.2, and v0.3.0 ships an older variant. Copy that one module into the project with the Apache-2.0 notice; it needs only numpy and scipy. Use the report's sketch and synthetic tests as unit tests, and widen the warp range, since the current test never makes live faster than ref.

2) Do not treat the TIMIT PPG as required. The same paper's online Chroma+MFCC(5) gets AAE 453 ms and median 144 ms, against 376/136 for Chroma+Phoneme5, with no trained model. That is the right day-one, license-free baseline for both modes. A multilingual phonetic feature for vocal-only mode (b) can be added later as an improvement.

3) The user is an explicit collaborator on the private repo and has a KAIST email, so asking Jiyun Park or MACLab for permission, or for a LICENSE, is a short conversation rather than a blocker. Even with permission, the English-read-speech TIMIT model is the wrong acoustic model for Korean/Japanese singing and full mixes.

Also carry forward:
- The reference steps in 160 ms blocks and its run limit is effectively absent (30+ blocks). Use per-frame steps with run limit 3, as Dixon and pymatchmaker do.
- Keep synctoolbox, which needs librosa<1.0 and numpy<2.5, in a separate offline/ground-truth environment if the live app moves to librosa 1.0.
missed_options: Vendor pymatchmaker's develop-branch OnlineTimeWarpingDixonFrame (Apache-2.0, same author, Java-MATCH-validated, already fixes the reference's DP bugs) instead of writing a new OLTW. pymatchmaker also has an Arzt-style OLTW (oltw_arzt.py) and HMM/particle-filter followers to compare against.
Use Chroma + MFCC(5) as the license-free feature baseline (paper Table 1: online AAE 453 ms, median 144 ms) before investing in a new PPG model.

Ask the author directly. The user is a listed collaborator (sjsjcircle) with a KAIST email; ask for a LICENSE file or written permission, and possibly the unpublished label-map and training code for the CRNN.
Use Dixon's original MATCH (Java) or the match-vamp port as a reference oracle for validating any OLTW reimplementation. pymatchmaker already did this, but note GPL if code is copied.

Replace the TIMIT 5-class PPG with a multilingual phonetic or self-supervised speech feature for vocal-only mode (b). The repo's unused whisper_reference.py shows the authors already tried Whisper-encoder features.

Build Korean/Japanese pseudo ground truth by forced-aligning the separated vocal stem to the lyric syllables. This uses the project's own offline pipeline instead of MusicXML→synctoolbox, plus a small hand-checked subset.

Treat the reference's warm-up differently: start detection or global re-localisation (e.g., a coarse subsequence-DTW search over the whole ref on the first few seconds and after loss) instead of a fixed lock-step band.
